A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Effort detector despite the changed title and organization. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original deepfake and synthetic-image detection experiments, ablations, robustness tests, and feature analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original detection experiments and supplementary evaluations and reports additional PCA and pre-training feature visualizations.

M1.justification: Equations 1–7 and Algorithm 1 retain the same procedure: freeze the principal SVD components, train the residual components, and apply classification, orthogonality, and singular-value constraints. Replacing semantic-knowledge terminology with pre-trained-knowledge terminology does not change the method.

E1.justification: v2 removes the dedicated FF++ c40 compressed-video evaluation from v1 Appendix B.3/Table 11, narrowing coverage of compression conditions. The principal deepfake datasets, DF40 manipulations, UniversalFakeDetect, GenImage, and separate perturbation tests remain.

E2.justification: TALL disappears from the cross-dataset and cross-method comparisons in Table 1, although TALL-Swin remains in the appendix video-detector comparison. The LoRA, MoE-LoRA, and Dual-Adapter comparisons already appeared in v1; their appearance in v2's main text is relocation.

E3.justification: The new PCA comparison uses the minimum component count explaining at least 90% variance, and the new t-SNE visualization adds a pre-training control. The loss ablation's averaging set shrinks from four datasets to CDF-v2 and SimSwap. Standard training settings and principal benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The diagnostic evidence is substantially reworked. v2 adds PCA retention comparisons and pre-training t-SNE analyses (Figures 5 and 8), but removes v1's deepfake rank-sensitivity study, dedicated within-domain compression comparison, and logit/confidence-distribution analysis. The loss ablation also loses its DFDC and FSGAN evaluations. Existing synthetic-image rank and adapter studies are retained through relocation.

E5.justification: Empirical benchmark results remain point estimates without reported seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The PCA variance analyses do not introduce uncertainty estimates for detection performance.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark scores match, including 95.19% mAcc and 99.41% mAP on UniversalFakeDetect. v2 adds PCA counts of 160 for original CLIP, 159 for Effort, 137 for LoRA, and 57 for full fine-tuning, plus initial-feature findings. Removed comparisons and ablations lose their result entries. The complete-method loss-ablation average changes from 0.921 to 0.941 because it averages two datasets instead of four, not because matched scores improve.

T1.justification: v2 adds Definition 3.1's covariance-rank asymmetry measure, Theorem 3.2's probabilistic lower bound with generator-rank assumptions, and an Appendix A proof. v1 contains the SVD method mathematics but no corresponding formal asymmetry theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims of efficient, generalizable detection through orthogonal adaptation remain. v2 additionally claims theoretical grounding for asymmetry and presents rank preservation more prominently in the abstract and contributions. Rank-collapse explanations and superiority over adapters were already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds an interpretation of SVD as the main source of ablation gains, with complementary benefits from the constraints, and interprets the new PCA comparison as information retention. Its Impact Statements add possible misuse to improve generators and proposed access controls. The original single-fake-class limitation and incremental-learning plans remain.

D1.justification: v2 drops v1's explicit default-rank selection rationale and trainable parameter counts for alternative deepfake ranks. Tables 2–3 newly mark NPR results as obtained from official models or reproduction. Core implementation details and the promise to release code and checkpoints upon acceptance remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Gunasekar et al. (2017) to support its rank/generalization rationale, Ding et al. (2023) for parameter-efficient tuning, and Fu et al. (2025) in related work. The substantive comparison with LoRA and other adapters already existed in v1 Appendix B.4.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, and analysis narrative are extensively rewritten around rank preservation. The separate motivation questions disappear, adapter discussion moves into the main text, and the appendices are reorganized. The title, author information, terminology, and citation style also change.

P2.justification: v2 substantially redistributes figures and tables. v1's PCA variance panels become introductory Figure 3, adapter and synthetic-rank tables move into the main text, and new Figures 5 and 8 appear. The conceptual diagram and confidence-distribution figure disappear, the loss table loses columns, and headers and caption placement change throughout. Existing synthetic-image t-SNE results remain in the appendix.

improvement.justification: The reorganization and new diagnostics improve accessibility, but v2 introduces reliability problems. Appendix A does not justify converting its nuclear-norm bound into the claimed rank bound, despite stronger theoretical claims. Figure 5 also equates component-count retention with variance retention without establishing that equivalence. Section 4.3 quotes obsolete four-dataset averages, including 0.921, while Table 4 now reports 0.941 over two datasets. These localized losses in rigor and consistency outweigh the presentation gains; the method and principal benchmark results remain intact.
